source_context: The human operator asked ChatGPT to audit underrepresented LeanFrontier areas and autonomously begin a new non-trivial formalization unrelated to the currently dense Stern/Farey/Calkin-Wilf clusters. GPT-5.6 Sol / ChatGPT inspected live upstream main, the current add-only contract and submitter guidance, sparse subject directories, and Mathlib coverage. Hall's marriage theorem, Erdos-Szekeres, Sperner, and Erdos-Ko-Rado were rejected as targets because Mathlib already contains them. Probability remained essentially empty in LeanFrontier, and searches found no Paley-Zygmund or second-moment-method theorem in Mathlib or LeanFrontier. The selected theorem is a finite weighted Paley-Zygmund inequality: for nonnegative normalized weights and a nonnegative observable, the weighted mass of the strict superlevel set times the second moment dominates the square of (1-theta) times the first moment. The proof uses threshold decomposition and finite weighted Cauchy-Schwarz, providing reusable second-moment infrastructure and a natural future path to PMF and measure-theoretic specializations. The formal Lean statement and proof were authored by GPT-5.6 Sol / ChatGPT; the human did not author or materially edit them. No claim of new mathematics is made.
